rules.title: Notice to Determine Estate at Will for Nonpayment of Rent
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent on an estate at will, a landlord must provide fourteen days' written notice to quit. However, if a tenant has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months, the tenant may prevent termination by paying or tendering the full amount of rent due within ten days of receiving the notice. Every such notice must contain specific statutory notification language informing the tenant of this right; failure to include such notification extends the tenant's payment period to the day an answer is due in any possession action.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to estates at will where tenant has failed or refused to pay rent; tenant may prevent termination by paying full rent due within ten days if no similar notice received in preceding twelve months
rules.exemptions: Tenant who has not received a similar notice to quit for nonpayment within the twelve months preceding receipt of current notice may prevent termination by paying or tendering full rent due within ten days
rules.conflict_note: Notice requirement extended if statutory notification language omitted from initial notice
rules.sanctions: Failure to include required notification extends tenant's cure period to the day answer is due in possession action; otherwise failure does not affect notice validity

rules.title: Notice to Terminate Estate at Will—General
rules.requirement: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' written notice. If rent is payable at periods of less than three months, the required notice period equals the interval between rent payment days or thirty days, whichever is longer. Such written notice may include an offer to establish a new tenancy on different terms, and inclusion of such offer does not affect the notice's validity.
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all estates at will in Massachusetts; notice required from either landlord or tenant

rules.title: Eviction Relief for Rent Nonpayment Caused by Government Benefit Delay
rules.requirement: When nonpayment of rent results from failure or delay by the federal government, the Commonwealth, a municipality, or their respective departments, agencies, or authorities in mailing or delivering subsistence or rental payments, checks, or vouchers (other than salary payments) to tenant or landlord, the court in any possession action shall continue the hearing not less than seven days to provide notice to the appropriate agency. If all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, is tendered to the landlord within that time period, the tenancy shall not be treated as terminated.
rules.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any action for possession shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when nonpayment is caused by federal government, Commonwealth, municipality, or their departments, agencies, or authorities failing or delaying in mailing or delivery of subsistence or rental payments, checks, or vouchers (excluding salary payments)
rules.sanctions: Court must continue hearing not less than seven days; if all rent due with interest and costs of suit is tendered within such time, tenancy is not treated as having been terminated
